index.title: AstroDeck | Plan and run your imaging night
index.description: Plan targets, build an imaging flow and watch your rig from a browser. Use AstroDeck on its own or alongside the setup you already have.
index.hero: Give your imaging night a plan.
index.intro: Choose your targets, set the sequence and follow each exposure from a browser. AstroDeck brings planning, capture and the night's progress into one place.

sections.heading: Start with the rig you have.
sections.text: Choose how AstroDeck fits your night.

cards.heading: Alongside NINA
cards.text: Connect through NINA's Advanced API plugin. NINA keeps the equipment connection while AstroDeck adds a browser interface, Flows and session progress.

cards.heading: Alongside ASIAIR
cards.text: Use AstroDeck's atlas and weather tools to plan a night while ASIAIR runs the rig. Keep capture and guiding in the ASIAIR app.

cards.heading: On its own
cards.text: Connect supported native drivers, ASCOM Alpaca devices or Windows ASCOM drivers. AstroDeck can handle capture, focus, guiding and the sequence.

sections.heading: See the whole night before you start.
sections.text: Connect targets to focus, guiding and capture steps. Add a cloud hold or an end-of-night park, then check the plan before you run it.
sections.imageAlt: AstroDeck Flows mosaic editor with simulator equipment in red night mode.
sections.imageCaption: A mosaic plan in Flows, shown with a simulator rig in red night mode.

sections.heading: Keep track of what the night has earned.
sections.text: Watch frame progress and guiding, then review the images that counted. Multi-night sessions retain accepted frames so you can return to an unfinished target.
sections.imageAlt: AstroDeck Monitor after a single simulated exposure, with no sequence running.
sections.imageCaption: Monitor after a single simulated exposure. No sequence is running, and weather monitoring is off.

cards.heading: Frame the target
cards.text: Use survey imagery and your field of view to compose a target or lay out a mosaic.

cards.heading: Follow the conditions
cards.text: Compare the forecast with frame-based cloud detection. Satellite cloud estimates are available within the GOES footprint.

cards.heading: Return to the session
cards.text: Review accepted and rejected frames, adjust a grade and continue the work across nights.

sections.heading: Meet AstroDeck on a simulated rig.
sections.text: Connect the simulator, take an exposure and try a short flow before you use real equipment.

sections.heading: Read the code. Check the fit.
sections.text: AstroDeck is under active development. Check the hardware notes and release assets for the path you plan to use.

features.title: AstroDeck features
features.description: Explore planning, capture, guiding and multi-night sessions. Check which tools depend on your connected devices and installed providers.
features.hero: From the first target to the last frame.
features.intro: Plan the field, capture the sequence and review the result. Available controls follow the devices and providers you connect.

sections.heading: Choose a field worth returning to.
sections.text: Search the sky atlas, place your camera's field of view on survey imagery and rotate the composition. Lay out a mosaic, then send the framing into a flow.

cards.heading: Tonight
cards.text: Compare target visibility and moon separation before you choose the night's work.

cards.heading: Offline survey imagery
cards.text: The Atlas has a schematic sky for offline use. Fetch survey tiles from inside the Atlas on your own machine before you need photographic imagery without a network.

sections.note: DSS2 imagery (c) AAO/STScI, served from CDS/ESA HiPS mirrors.

sections.heading: Inspect the exposure as it arrives.
sections.text: View a stretched preview, examine the histogram and save linear FITS data. Live stacking combines incoming frames for a running view of the target.

cards.heading: Focus
cards.text: Run autofocus with an available provider, review the focus curve and set refocus triggers for the sequence.

cards.heading: Guide
cards.text: Use the native guide engine, PHD2 or NINA's guiding connection. Follow the error graph and use dithering in a sequence.

cards.heading: Calibration
cards.text: Build and match calibration masters. Flat auto-exposure and dusk-flat steps are available for a compatible setup.

sections.heading: Make a repeatable plan for the night.
sections.text: Flows connects targets with capture, focus and guiding steps. Add filter cycles, weather holds and a planned shutdown. The plan checker reports wiring and settings that need attention.

sections.heading: Keep the frames that count.
sections.text: The session ledger records frame quality and acceptance. Review grades, override a decision and continue an unfinished session across nights. Reports and export bundles keep the result together.

sections.heading: Stay close to the rig from a browser.
sections.text: Watch progress, camera cooling and guide performance on the monitor. Configure notifications through ntfy, Telegram or a webhook. Optional relay access connects outward from the rig.

cards.heading: Access for the people using it
cards.text: Viewer, operator and admin roles control access. Local accounts and Google sign-in are available.

cards.heading: At the telescope
cards.text: Use the interface on a phone or tablet, with dark-adaptation mode and brightness controls.

sections.heading: Check the provider as well as the device.
sections.text: Native guiding and native autofocus require astrodeck_native, which published releases do not include yet. Native polar alignment also depends on that engine. ASTAP plate solving needs a separate solver and star database. Hardware controls such as cooling, rotation and power switching depend on the driver and device.

flows.title: Astro Flows | Plan an imaging night
flows.description: Build an imaging plan with targets, mosaics, filter cycles and weather rules. Check it, run it and continue the session across nights.
flows.hero: Put the night on a canvas.
flows.intro: Start with a target and connect the work around it. Flows keeps the sequence visible, from the first focus run to the end-of-night park.

sections.heading: A target can be one frame or a mosaic.
sections.text: Frame the target on survey imagery, set the panel grid and choose how to visit the panels. Capture and filter-cycle steps can work through each panel or rotate through the mosaic in passes.
sections.imageAlt: AstroDeck Flows mosaic editor with simulator equipment in red night mode.
sections.imageCaption: A mosaic plan in Flows, shown with a simulator rig in red night mode.

sections.heading: Connect the sequence and its reactions.

cards.heading: Flow wires
cards.text: Solid wires set the order of work, such as a target followed by autofocus, guiding and capture.

cards.heading: Event wires
cards.text: Dashed wires carry events to actions. A frame-quality condition can request refocus; a cloud event can put the sequence on hold.

sections.text: FILTER CYCLE interleaves exposures across filters so each channel receives time during the night.

sections.heading: Check the plan before it runs.
sections.text: The plan checker reports missing connections, conflicts between safety and cloud rules, and settings the engine cannot use. Review those messages alongside the equipment and provider requirements.

sections.heading: Give cloud and unsafe conditions different responses.

cards.heading: Pause for cloud
cards.text: A cloud hold can wait for clear frames, then restore cooling and the imaging setup before continuing. Set a maximum wait and the action to take when it expires.

cards.heading: End on unsafe conditions
cards.text: A safety monitor can abort the sequence and request a park. Roof and cover actions depend on your configuration and connected equipment.

sections.heading: Return to the work still owed.
sections.text: New target blocks count accepted frames. A session retains progress across nights, and repeat schedules can return at dusk. Target pools choose among the targets that remain available.

sections.heading: Begin with an example.
sections.text: The example library includes single-target imaging, filter cycles, campaigns and a mosaic. Open one to see its structure, then make a copy for your own rig.
sections.linkLabel: Try a flow with the simulator

hardware.title: AstroDeck hardware and compatibility
hardware.description: Native drivers, ASCOM Alpaca, Windows ASCOM, NINA and the experimental ASIAIR backend. Separate driver support from documented device checks.
hardware.hero: Check the connection before the clear night.
hardware.intro: AstroDeck works through native drivers, ASCOM Alpaca and software backends. A driver's supported device family is broader than the hardware checked on this project.

sections.heading: Native device drivers
sections.text: Native drivers use vendor SDKs or serial protocols. Verified below means the named check is recorded for that device. Supported means an implemented driver path, without the same recorded check. Neither label certifies every control or a full unattended night.

rows: Native movement and tracking checks are recorded for an AM5N.
The family driver exists; the recorded native validation names the AM5N.
SDK properties and gain checks are recorded. Native cooler and anti-dew control are not implemented.
The native adapter discovers SDK-listed cameras. Native cooler and anti-dew control are not implemented.
SDK properties, gain and sensor-mode checks are recorded. Fetch the SDK on your machine.
Controls follow reported capabilities. Fetch the SDK on your machine.
Recorded hardware inventory identifies an EAF. The driver implements movement, position and temperature.
Recorded hardware inventory identifies a CAA. The driver implements rotation controls.
The wheel's serial protocol is recorded as checked on hardware.

sections.note: Verification is limited to the check named in each row. SDK enumeration, a connected device and a completed imaging night are different evidence.

sections.heading: ASCOM connections

cards.heading: ASCOM Alpaca
cards.text: Connect compatible network devices and assign their roles. AstroDeck has adapters for cameras, mounts, focusers, filter wheels, rotators, domes, safety monitors, switches and cover calibrators.

cards.heading: Windows ASCOM drivers
cards.text: The local COM-to-Alpaca host can expose installed Windows ASCOM drivers to AstroDeck. It requires the relevant ASCOM driver and the optional COM host dependency.

sections.note: Protocol support does not verify a particular manufacturer's driver. Check the controls your device exposes.

sections.heading: Alongside NINA
sections.text: NINA's Advanced API plugin provides the connection. AstroDeck's backend exposes camera, mount, focuser, filter wheel, rotator, switch and guider roles. NINA keeps the hardware connection.

sections.heading: Alongside ASIAIR
sections.text: You can use AstroDeck's planning and weather tools while ASIAIR runs the rig. An optional experimental backend also exists for ASIAIR's proprietary network protocol through libasi.
bullets: The backend exposes camera, mount, focuser and switch roles.
It does not provide filter-wheel, rotator or guider roles. Guiding remains in ASIAIR.
The adapter checks whether the box is busy before changing state.
The repository tests use a fake transport; full AstroDeck operation on an ASIAIR is not established by those tests.
Source installs require the asiair extra, which installs libasi from its repository.
sections.note: This is not an official ASIAIR API integration. Treat the optional backend as experimental.

sections.heading: Imaging providers

rows: ASTAP and a compatible star database, or NINA's solver when available.
AstroDeck native engine or a supported backend provider.
AstroDeck native engine, PHD2 or NINA's guider connection.
AstroDeck native engine or NINA TPPA when its prerequisites are present.

sections.note: Native guiding and native autofocus require astrodeck_native, which published releases do not include yet. See issue #630 for release packaging status.

sections.heading: Host platforms
sections.text: The release workflow targets Windows x86-64, Linux x86-64, Linux arm64 and macOS arm64. Orange Pi 5 Pro appliance tooling is a separate setup path. Check a release's asset list before choosing a download.

sections.heading: Tell us about missing hardware.
sections.text: Open an issue with the vendor, model and connection method. Include the driver or protocol documentation if you have it. Third-party backends can register through the package entry-point interface.

weather.title: AstroDeck weather awareness
weather.description: Compare forecasts, satellite cloud estimates and your own frames. Understand cloud holds, safety stops and the limits of satellite coverage.
weather.hero: Keep the sky in the plan.
weather.intro: Use the forecast to plan ahead, satellite imagery to inspect nearby cloud and your own exposures to judge the view through the telescope.

sections.heading: Read each source for what it can tell you.

cards.heading: Forecast
cards.text: Open-Meteo supplies forecast data. Astrospheric requires your own eligible account, API key and the in-app acknowledgement. Available forecast fields depend on the provider.

cards.heading: Satellite cloud estimates
cards.text: GOES cloud-mask and cloud-top data are projected into a sky dome. Successive observations support short-term drift estimates, with the source time and availability shown.

cards.heading: Your own frames
cards.text: Bright-star counts and image contrast feed a cloud score. Exposure, focus and your rig's thresholds affect the result, so the sequence uses a debounced reading.

sections.heading: Check coverage before relying on the dome.
sections.text: The satellite layer uses GOES-18 and GOES-19 and is intended for sites within their footprint, principally the Americas. Outside coverage, or with missing or stale data, the service reports the limitation. Forecast and frame-based checks are separate from that satellite coverage.
sections.note: Satellite cloud mapping needs the optional cloudmap dependency, a configured observing site and network access to fetch observations.

sections.heading: Let a passing cloud pause the sequence.
sections.text: With a cloud-hold rule configured, the sequence stops normal capture and probes for clearing. It can collect configured hold darks while waiting. Before resuming, it restores the filter and checks cooling, centring and guiding as required.
sections.note: Set the maximum hold and timeout action in the plan. These behaviors require the relevant connected equipment and providers.

sections.heading: Keep safety decisions separate.
sections.text: A connected safety monitor can end the sequence on an unsafe or stale reading. Parking and closure follow the configured shutdown behavior. Satellite estimates are advisory and do not operate the safety gate.

sections.heading: Check the forecast again at dusk.
sections.text: Automatic session re-arming can wait when the forecast predicts rain. Forecast cloud cover is shown for planning and does not veto the night. Review the weather settings and any override before leaving a repeating plan armed.

getting-started.title: Get started with AstroDeck
getting-started.description: Start on Windows or Linux arm64, try the simulator, and check the requirements for NINA or an Orange Pi 5 Pro appliance.
getting-started.hero: Start with a browser and a simulated rig.
getting-started.intro: Choose a setup path, open AstroDeck locally and try a short exposure. Add real equipment after checking the drivers and imaging providers you need.

sections.heading: Windows: run the release executable.
sections.text: Open the release asset list and look for astrodeck-windows-x86_64.exe. Download the matching SHA-256 file, check the download and run the executable as your normal Windows user. It serves the browser interface without a separate Python or Node installation.
steps: Run the executable from a folder you can access. Keep its console open while AstroDeck is running.
Open http://localhost:8800 on the same computer.
Use the simulator steps below to try the interface.

For real equipment, check the driver and provider requirements. Native guiding and native autofocus require astrodeck_native, which published releases do not include yet. Install ASTAP separately for local plate solving.
sections.note: The standalone executable stores configuration and captures under %LOCALAPPDATA%\AstroDeck by default. Configuration requires NTFS or ReFS. This is a standalone executable, not a Windows installer.

sections.heading: Take the first exposure on a simulator.
steps: Open Equipment, or Rig > Devices in the newer interface, and choose the simulator action.
Open Capture, set a short exposure and take a frame.
Open Flows and inspect an example. Make a copy before changing it.
Run a short plan and review its progress and frames.
sections.text: The simulated camera responds to pointing, focus and filters. It lets you explore the workflow without connecting physical equipment.
sections.note: Set an observing site before using visibility and scheduling tools. For a demonstration, use a location you are comfortable sharing.

sections.heading: Connect an existing NINA setup.
steps: Install and enable NINA's Advanced API plugin on the computer running NINA.
In AstroDeck, add a NINA driver using that computer's host and the plugin's configured port. The backend default is 1888.
Assign the available NINA devices to roles and connect the rig.
sections.text: Use AstroDeck's browser interface and Flows while NINA maintains the equipment connection. Available roles are listed on the hardware page.

sections.heading: Orange Pi 5 Pro: distinguish Linux from appliance setup.
sections.text: For an existing 64-bit Linux installation, the release workflow targets a linux-arm64 executable. Check the release assets and the device SDKs for that environment. Appliance provisioning is a separate path for a commissioned Orange Pi 5 Pro.
steps: On an already commissioned appliance, use the setup network and unique password printed for that board when an onboarding window is authorized.
Connect to the AstroDeck-XXXX setup network and open http://10.42.0.1/ if the portal does not appear.
Choose the home Wi-Fi network and enter its credentials.
Open the appliance on the joined network using the address provided for the board.
sections.note: The setup hotspot is limited to a 15-minute authorized window. There is no shared fallback password. The repository contains provisioning tooling, not a generally downloadable, ready-to-flash appliance image.

sections.heading: Build from source when you need optional components.
sections.text: A source checkout needs Python 3.11 or newer. Building the web interface uses Node 20 or newer. On Windows, these commands create an environment and install the COM host and cloudmap extras.
sections.code:
git clone https://github.com/epim/astrodeck.git
cd astrodeck
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -e "./server[comhost,cloudmap]"
npm --prefix ui ci
npm --prefix ui run build
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m astrodeck
sections.note: For AstroDeck native autofocus, guiding and polar alignment, build and install the Rust extension in the same Python environment. ASTAP and its star database are separate from that extension. The ASIAIR extra is optional and experimental.

sections.heading: Open the interface from another device.
sections.text: A fresh instance binds to localhost. Create an admin account before allowing network access. The create-admin command prompts for a password and enables local sign-in.
sections.note: Use the host computer's address and port 8800 from a phone or tablet on the same network. Keep the application running as a normal user.

releases.title: AstroDeck releases
releases.description: Find AstroDeck release notes, platform assets and checksums. Check the contents and prerequisites for the build you choose.
releases.hero: Choose a build for your setup.
releases.intro: GitHub Releases holds the release notes and downloadable assets. Use the files attached to the release you choose; the source version and available downloads can differ.

sections.heading: Match the operating system and architecture.
sections.text: These are the release workflow's target names. Confirm that your chosen release includes the file and its SHA-256 sidecar before downloading.

sections.heading: Recent release records
sections.text: These summaries follow release commits and deployment notes in the repository. Check GitHub Releases for available downloads.

cards.text: Fixed session recovery, guide-pulse handling and report retries, and updated Flows and Monitor controls. Deployment now checks dependency floors.
Added fixes for lost mount connections, sun checks, alert delivery and privacy in logs and reports, alongside findings from the first mosaic run.
Uses the solve filter for rotation checks and accepts a rotation that stops within the mosaic's angle tolerance.
Added the mosaic Target editor and canvas, run and Continue controls, phone readouts and Send to Flow Wizard entry points.

sections.heading: Check what the build contains.
bullets: The standalone executable includes the browser interface and Python runtime.
Native guiding and native autofocus require astrodeck_native, which published releases do not include yet. Follow issue #630 for packaging status.
ASTAP plate solving requires the solver and its star database.
The Atlas has an offline schematic sky. Fetch survey tiles from inside the Atlas on your own machine before you need photographic imagery offline.
sections.note: DSS2 imagery (c) AAO/STScI, served from CDS/ESA HiPS mirrors.

sections.heading: Keep the update path clear.
sections.text: For a standalone executable, stop AstroDeck and replace the file; its default configuration and capture directories live separately. Supervised installations have a signed update path with health checks and rollback.
sections.note: The release tarball has Ed25519 signature and SHA-256 sidecars. That signature is separate from operating-system code signing for a standalone executable.

sections.heading: Read the changes behind a release.
sections.text: Review the release notes for fixes and changes that affect your rig. The source repository includes implementation details, tests and third-party notices.
